Alright, I've been mining the chat history across multiple servers to collect any technical ideas that could be relevant for our ongoing research on model scaling, expert mixtures, and training strategies. So far I've queried the main “general” channels on the two biggest guilds, as well as the “general-minimythos” and “general-1” channels, and also the “💬☼general-discussion” channel which is a catch‑all for broader ML discussion. Those searches returned a decent amount of content, but I still haven't covered all the side‑project or staff channels that might contain more niche or higher‑level brainstorming.

Looking back at the `chat_history.json` structure, each entry has a `name` field for the channel name and a `guild_id`. The earlier queries used `select(.value.name==\"general-minimythos\")` or similar exact matches. However, there are also channels whose names include substrings like “sideprojects”, “lobby”, or “staff”. These are likely to hold discussions about experimental ideas, internal planning, or even meta‑discussions about distillation, tokenization, loops, latent reasoning, experts, recursion, synthetic data, pretraining curricula, ternary representations, embedding growth, and architectural concepts. The previous greps were fairly specific, but they missed these channels because they weren't explicitly listed.

To capture those, I need to broaden the selection criteria. Using `select(.value.name|test(\"sideprojects|lobby|staff\"))` will match any channel whose name contains any of those substrings, regardless of case sensitivity (the default regex is case‑sensitive, but the channel names are likely lower‑case). Then, I should pull out each message’s author and content, and filter for the key technical keywords I've been tracking: `distill`, `tokeni` (to catch tokenization), `loop`, `latent`, `expert`, `recursi` (for recursion), `synthetic`, `pretrain`, `curricul` (curriculum), `ternary`, `embedding`, `grow`, as well as phrases like `arch idea` or `what if`. This mirrors the earlier grep patterns.

I also need to exclude any lines that are just empty author entries (e.g., “User:” with no content), which the previous pattern did with `grep -vE '^[^:]+: *$'`. Finally, to keep the output manageable, I’ll limit it to the first 80 matches using `head -80`.

Putting it all together, the appropriate Bash command is:

`cd /home/lane/Blindbot && jq -r 'to_entries[] | select(.value.name|test(\"sideprojects|lobby|staff\")) | .value.messages[] | \"\\(.author): \\(.content)\"' chat_history.json | grep -iE 'distill|tokeni|loop|latent|expert|recursi|synthetic|pretrain|curricul|ternary|embedding|grow|arch idea|what if' | grep -vE '^[^:]+: *$' | head -80`

This will give me a concise set of potentially valuable ideas from the remaining channels that haven't been examined yet. Executing this will bring the missing pieces into our knowledge base, allowing us to further synthesize and prioritize the collected concepts.
